question:
A 75-year-old man is evaluated for a 9-month history of altered bowel habits and recent blood in his
stool. His medical history includes hypertension managed with lisinopril. Vital signs include a blood
pressure of 141/93 mm Hg, heart rate of 78/min, respiratory rate of 13/min, and temperature of 37.5°C
(99.5°F). On examination, the patient appears anxious, and a palpable mass is detected in the left
lower quadrant of the abdomen. Colonoscopy reveals a neoplasm in the descending colon, and biopsy
confirms colorectal cancer. Based on this diagnosis, where is the most likely location of a discrete area

of tenderness in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Right lateral thigh and posterior to the iliotibial band
(B) Distal left tibia (C) Left lower rib cage (D) Lumbosacral spine (E) Right proximal humerus (F)
Midshaft of the left femur (G) Proximal left femur (H) Left ischial tuberosity (I) Right iliac crest (J) Left
greater trochanter
 A. Distal left tibia
B. Left greater trochanter
C. Right proximal humerus
D. Lumbosacral spine
E. Proximal left femur
F. Left lower rib cage
G. Left ischial tuberosity
H. Right iliac crest
I. Right lateral thigh and posterior to the iliotibial band
J. Midshaft of the left femur
